newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND GAMES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league (kick-off times 1500 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Blackburn Rovers (17) v Middlesbrough (16)

Blackburn will be boosted by Tuesday's news that Swede Sven Goran Eriksson will be their new manager from the end of the season but meanwhile caretaker manager Tony Parkes needs to get Rovers back to winning ways against Middlesbrough. Goalkeeper Tim Flowers is ready to return after a hamstring injury although Shay Given may keep his place. Injury-plagued Middlesbrough will be looking for their first victory since September 14 but will be without Nigel Pearson, Steve Vickers, Curtis Fleming, Phil Stamp and Robbie Mustoe.
Chelsea (8) v West Ham United (15)

Chelsea will be aiming to recover from Sunday's 3-0 defeat at Sunderland although they will be without French defender Frank LeBeouf and midfield captain Dennis Wise who are both suspended. West Ham, knocked out of the League Cup by second division Stockport on Wednesday, may be without Tim Breacker and Stan Lazaridis.
Everton (7) v Leeds (13)

Everton, beaten only once in their last 11 league games, will be looking to continue this run against Leeds. Everton are likely to have midfielder Tony Grant available after his swift recovery from an ankle injury, while fellow midfielder John Ebbrell will be sidelined until the New Year with a hairline fracture of the foot.
Leeds will be without ex-Manchester United star Lee Sharpe, who has a hamstring injury, and recent 400,000 pounds signing Gunnar Halle will take his place on the left of midfield.
Leicester (12) v Coventry (19)

Coventry will be aiming to build on Tuesday's 2-1 victory over Newcastle, only their second win of the season and the first since new manager Gordon Strachan took over. Leicester have not played for two weeks since drawing 1-1 at home to Blackburn.
Manchester United (6) v Sunderland (14)

Manchester United are set to recall England midfielder David Beckham, who was rested from the starting line-up for Wednesday's 1-1 draw with Sheffield Wednesday before making a brief second- half substitute appearance. United are currently nine points behind leaders Liverpool and in need of a resurgence in form to protect their hold on the championship.

Sunderland, boosted by a 3-0 victory over Chelsea, are expected to be unchanged, with regular right-back Polish Dariusz Kubicki again starting on the left and Gareth Hall keeping his position on the right.
Nottingham Forest (20) v Arsenal (2)

New caretaker player-manager Stuart Pearce has a tough test against in-form Arsenal. Forest are without a victory in 16 premier league games. Defender Steve Chettle is hoping to recover from influenza and midfielder Chris Bart-Williams' hamstring strain rules him out. Arsenal are boosted by the return of Dutch striker Dennis Bergkamp, who scored for the Netherlands in Belgium last weekend, from a thigh problem. But Tony Adams and Patrick Vieira are both suspended.
Southampton (18) v Derby (11)

Southampton, without a win in their last five league games, will be without England midfielder Matt Le Tissier (thigh). Defenders Jason Dodd and Simon Charlton and Dutchman Ulrich van Gobbel are all suspended. Derby manager Jim Smith has a fully-fit squad at his disposal with striker Marco Gabbiadini now fully recovered from a minor cartilage operation.
Tottenham (10) v Sheffield Wednesday (9)
Tottenham's two recent signings of 2.5 million pounds Norwegian Stefan Iversen and 2.6 million pounds defender John Scales are likely to be make their White Hart Lane home debuts.

England midfielder Darren Anderton is expected to be sidelined for another two weeks with a knee injury while forward Chris Armstrong underwent an operation on his ankle and is hoped to return in five weeks. Defender Justin Edinburgh is suspended.
Sheffield Wednesday are unbeaten in eight games, six of which have been drawn.
Sunday
1600 gmt
Aston Villa (5) v Wimbledon (3)

This fixture brings together two in-form sides with Aston Villa having won their last four games. Australian international goalkeeper Mark Bosnich is fit again but manager Brian Little may decide to stick with Michael Oakes. England defender Gareth Southgate will be sidelined until the New Year with an ankle injury.
Wimbledon will be aiming to extend their run of 19 games unbeaten and welcome back captain Vinnie Jones who returns from international duty with Wales.
Monday
2000gmt
Newcastle (4) v Liverpool (1)
Doubts are being raised about Newcastle's championship prospects and a win against the league leaders is vital for Kevin Keegan's men who currently trail Liverpool by seven points.
